contract: Workspace-scoped IndexedDB recovery COPIES; acknowledgement required; restore always NEW unsaved note/to-do, never in-place update/replay. Four copies/twoMiB each/eightMiB logical total.

products/rea-studio/apps/notes/draft-rec: draft recovery scope persists for the same workspace, differs at the same origin for another workspace, and never edits saved notes
draft recovery public module delivery is byte exact and scope access retains the host token and origin boundaries
draft recovery records preserve exact editor text and creation type while adding only their explicit storage schema and scope
draft recovery validation keeps source identity as provenance and refuses inconsistent saved revisions, stale consent fields and foreign namespaces
draft recovery validation rejects malformed record types, unsafe versions and nonfinite clocks without mutating the caller
draft recovery record limits admit documented text boundaries and separately enforce UTF8 serialized bytes
draft recovery preserves unsaved fields and parent/type across a remount and creates no note until an acknowledged explicit Save
recovery provenance never becomes an in-place update even when the original note advanced to a newer revision
an unacknowledged committed first Save recovers only as an explicitly chosen separate copy after reload
an old held Save cannot clear or rewrite a newer editor recovery owner
quota and corrupt-list failures preserve the active draft and do not prevent explicit server Save
discarding an older displayed version cannot delete another tab newer recovery record
explicit recovery discard leaves the active editor intact and later typing starts a fresh recoverable identity
discard cancellation and exports preserve the unsaved recovery boundary without treating a copy as a saved item
rapid input retains at most one active storage write and one latest pending snapshot while preserving the final complete text
a delayed recovery-open read cannot replace later typing or a newly selected editor
a missing recovered notebook has an explicit default-Notes warning before a separate copy can be saved
